Short answer: The free first look is a decision aid. We listen, inspect the agreed public or owner-provided context, and tell you what to keep, fix, connect, replace, or investigate next.

What this means for your business

It is not permission to enter accounts, scan private systems, submit forms, or change production. The scope should name what we can see and what evidence the recommendation uses.

What to watch

  • A so-called audit that is only a sales deck.
  • A confident conclusion made without access or evidence.
  • Private credentials sent through an ordinary form.
  • A recommendation that ignores who owns or supports the result.

Do this next

  1. Describe the business problem and what it interrupts.
  2. Share public links or non-secret facts only.
  3. Choose the one decision the first look should help make.
  4. Review the written next step and any paid scope separately.

When Little Fight fits

Use the Tech Audit when the problem crosses tools or you do not know where it starts. For one obvious typo or cable, fix the typo or cable.

Start the free first look
